question_text: A student's web browser sends a request for a web page to a server on another network. Describe the role of each of the four layers of the TCP/IP model in sending this request, and how the layers interact so that the request arrives reliably.
adaptation_rationale: Original question written by Claude (single-agent Chunk 3 continuation, 2026-11-04) for a syllabus statement with no linked question at handover; no historical source question or official marking status claimed.
solution: Application layer: the browser uses an application protocol such as HTTP/HTTPS to create the request message. Transport layer: TCP splits the data into numbered segments, adds port numbers and sequence numbers, and uses acknowledgements and retransmission of lost segments (with checksums) so the receiver can reassemble complete, in-order data. Internet layer: IP places segments into packets with source and destination IP addresses and routers forward them across networks towards the destination. Network interface layer: packets are placed into frames with hardware (MAC) addresses and transmitted as signals over the physical medium (cable/Wi-Fi) on each link. Interaction: each layer encapsulates the data from the layer above by adding its own header and passes it down; at the server the layers remove the headers in reverse (decapsulation) and pass the data up to the web-server application.

marking_points.criterion: Application: creates the request using an application protocol (e.g. HTTP/HTTPS).
Transport: TCP divides data into segments with port numbers and sequence numbers.
Transport reliability: acknowledgements, retransmission of lost/corrupted segments and in-order reassembly.
Internet: IP adds source/destination IP addresses and packets are routed between networks.
Network interface: frames with MAC addresses are transmitted over the physical medium on each link.
Interaction: encapsulation down the stack (each layer adds a header) and decapsulation up the stack at the receiver.

acceptable_alternatives: Accept "link layer" for network interface. Accept checksums as part of reliability. Do not credit sequencing/reliability attributed to IP (internet layer).
partial_credit_notes: Award each independent point once, up to 6 marks. Accept equivalent correct wording or valid alternative code. Do not double-credit one idea.
